entry_kinds.id: the exact fact id must be present in tier1
entry_kinds.one_of: at least one of the listed fact ids must be present in tier1
entry_kinds.prefix: at least one tier1 fact id starting with the prefix must be present
entry_kinds.pairs: where the first id of a pair is present in tier1, the second must be too
entry_kinds.prefix_pairs: a family that only means anything in pairs: at least one tier1 fact id starting with `prefix` must be present, and every one of them must carry its companion - the same id with `companion_prefix` in place of `prefix`. What management guided for a quarter says nothing on its own; beside what it delivered it says whether management hits its own numbers
entry_kinds.parallel_prefixes: every listed prefix must be present in tier1 AND the suffixes after the prefixes must be the SAME SET across all of them - a repeated structure (one row per cycle, one row per venue) is complete or it is not there; an optional min_members says how many members the structure needs before it is a structure at all
entry_kinds.requires_arithmetic: the fact IS built from other facts in the pack, so it must declare its arithmetic and the gate recomputes it - a claimed difference is asserted, not shown. The companion `arithmetic` names the operation and the operand fact ids IN ORDER, because a capture that adds where the anchor subtracts would otherwise have its own wrong sum faithfully verified
entry_kinds.substitute: AB19 as AB20 reshapes it, capital spending ONLY: where the capture declares the named gap class as absent by design, the fact is a stand-in for a line the filer does not publish, and the ruling's machine-knowable terms bind - both years TAGGED as ceilings naming the SAME published line, struck by the same operation over the same number of operands, every operand of both a reading the capture actually carries, and each named free-cash-flow fact BOTH struck against its own year's ceiling AND tagged as a floor. The declaration is the capture's own bound tag, never words hunted out of a source sentence. Undeclared, the entry behaves as its level alone says - and a stand-in tag on the fact with no declared gap is itself refused, because AB19 requires the gap row alongside
entry_kinds.shapes: what each part of a prefix or parallel_prefixes floor must LOOK like to count, per prefix: its part name, its shape, the units it is admitted in (units) and what those units mean (units_mean). buy_or_sell reads exactly buy or sell; trade_date is an ISO date (YYYY-MM-DD) not after the capture and not more than window_days before it; positive_number is a number above zero whose as_of is not after the capture; a part in any unit outside its list is refused, named with its unit. EVERY fact matching the prefix is checked and any malformed one refuses by name, with one exception: under a prefix floor a fact of exactly zero, otherwise well-shaped, beside one that counts neither refuses nor counts. A prefix floor is met by one well-shaped fact; every member of a parallel_prefixes floor (named member_name and its suffix) must be well-shaped in all its parts, or it is not counted at all. Whether the figure is TRUE is a matter for the owner's review and the outside auditor
entry_kinds.levels: required = missing refuses; conditional = missing refuses unless a gap is declared with the stated reason; advisory = recorded, never refuses

revenue_families.why: AC12.3 (owner, 2026-09-08): a revenue line in the business frame may point ONLY at revenue. Before this rule a line could cite any fact the pack carried - the last price included - and the case file printed that id under the heading 'Facts that carry it', so a seat could argue the mix of the business from a number that is not revenue. Named here as DATA so the families can be widened by a ruling without touching code. A member of a basket or a theme carries the same ids under its own '__<ticker>' suffix; the gate strips that suffix before it reads this list.
revenue_families.derived: a derived fact counts as revenue where every operand it is struck from is itself revenue by this list, however many steps down - the share of the period a line carries is exactly such a fact

depth.why: AC41(1) as amended of record, and AC47: the depth of the insider evidence follows what officers and directors together own. The holder-structure test reads first the ownership percentage (a ceiling bound at or under the threshold reads under it, a floor bound at or over it reads at or over it), then the group's shares beside the shares in issue in the same unit, exactly and without division; under the threshold the floor is met by the three summary facts - the count of dealings, their net direction by shares, their total value bought plus sold over the twelve months - plus the chief executive's (both, where the company has two co-chief executives; a division head with the title never), the finance chief's and the chair's own dealings, each a whole dealing whose id ends in its role (ceo_<n>, cfo_<n>, chair_<n>); at or over it every dealing, as before; more is never less. A declared gap on the percentage decides nothing by itself. Where the ownership cannot be established - the percentage declared absent by design and no share counts that decide - the insider evidence is not considered: the floor does not apply, the pack carries no insider_flow_ fact, and the owner's pages and the seats' case file say so

asset_classes.authority: ANCHORLESS-SPEC sections 2 and 4 (owner rulings AB13.4 and AB15): the asset class decides the sufficiency anchor set and the rating basis, and nothing else. The class lists below are the owner's own confirmed lists, including the PBoC enhancement he added to gold's central-bank anchor. Later classes are ADDITIONS to this data, never code.

common_anchorless.note: Applied to EVERY anchorless class on top of its own list: the anchors the commissioned brief calls class-generic (the dated event calendar and five-year realized volatility; the price with its freshness rule sits in each class's own list, because the ruled ceiling differs by class) plus the cash rate, because ANCHORLESS-SPEC section 3 makes cash and the five-year volatility the two inputs of the rating bar itself. A pack that cannot answer the bar cannot earn a rating, which is the failure this unit exists to fix.

crypto.reading_rule: Every cohort figure here is read BESIDE the fund flows. Roughly 1.3 million coins now sit inside exchange-traded funds, custodied overwhelmingly by one firm, and a coin moving into fund custody resets its age to day one. In a heavy-creation period the coin-age split and the cost bases partly measure custody plumbing rather than investor behaviour - and the record says so rather than silently trusting them.

omitted.nupl: Net unrealised profit/loss is exactly one minus the reciprocal of MVRV - a rearrangement of a metric already required. Requiring both would let one fact vote twice.
omitted.whale_and_address_cohorts: An address is not a person. Fund custody compresses millions of owners into a handful of very large addresses, so 'whales are accumulating' now frequently means 'a fund had a creation'. The most corrupted family after the ETFs arrived, and the most likely to produce a confident wrong answer.
omitted.thermocap_stock_to_flow_pi_cycle: No mechanism. Thermocap divides by a quantity that only ever grows, so it is never actionable at a decision horizon; stock-to-flow was falsified in public; Pi-cycle and rainbow charts are curve-fits to three prior cycles.
omitted.active_addresses_and_nvt: Both assume on-chain transaction activity proxies economic activity. Most trading is now off-chain or inside fund wrappers, so it no longer does.

gold.note: ANCHORLESS-SPEC 4.B, confirmed by the owner at freeze with his PBoC enhancement (AB15), grounded in the commissioned gold/commodity brief of 2026-09-01. Gold is a MONETARY asset, not a commodity: essentially every ounce ever mined still exists and annual mine supply is about 1.5 per cent of that stock, so nothing on the supply side moves the price. The anchors answer one question - who is buying, why, and what would make them stop.

anchors.likely_source: the London bullion benchmark price as free JSON
anchors.why: ANCHORLESS-SPEC section 4: the price with its freshness rule - the class-generic anchor every anchorless subject carries

anchors.likely_source: the Federal Reserve's FRED, free CSV, no key, next business day
anchors.why: ANCHORLESS-SPEC 4.B.1: the five-year inflation-protected government bond yield - what the safe alternative pays. The textbook relationship has broken down since 2022, which is the argument for KEEPING the anchor: the ladder must say whether the bull case needs yields to fall, and if not, name the buyer paying up regardless

anchors.likely_source: the Federal Reserve's FRED, free CSV, no key, next business day

anchors.likely_source: the World Gold Council's free file, drawn from IMF statistics - the dashboard runs two to five months behind, so stamp the as-of date it actually carries
anchors.why: ANCHORLESS-SPEC 4.B.2: official-sector buying, the LATEST PUBLISHED QUARTER with its as-of date stamped. The buyer who does not care about price, and the most important driver of this market since 2022. A slow series by nature: its freshness rule is written for a slow series and the staleness is RENDERED beside it, never hidden

anchors.likely_source: the People's Bank of China's own reported reserve figures, dated
anchors.why: ANCHORLESS-SPEC 4.B.2, the owner's enhancement (ruling AB15): the PBoC IN ISOLATION - its OFFICIAL reported purchases. The one central bank with a special appetite for gold must never disappear into an average

anchors.why: ANCHORLESS-SPEC 4.B.2 (AB15): the dated MARKET ESTIMATE of the PBoC's true buying, carried beside the official figure

anchors.likely_source: the difference of the two facts above - declare the arithmetic so the gate recomputes it
anchors.why: ANCHORLESS-SPEC 4.B.2 (AB15): the DIVERGENCE made visible. The owner ruled that the gap between what the PBoC reports and what the market estimates it actually buys is itself information the council must see - so it is a fact on the page, not an invitation to subtract

anchors.why: ANCHORLESS-SPEC 4.B.3: gold fund holdings - what the Western investor owns

anchors.why: ANCHORLESS-SPEC 4.B.3: the monthly flow - is private money joining the move or selling into it?

anchors.why: ANCHORLESS-SPEC 4.B.4: speculative futures positioning - how crowded the trade is, and how much of the recent move is borrowed conviction that can reverse in a week

anchors.likely_source: FRED's BROAD dollar index, free and daily - never the popular index, which is over half euro and misleads
anchors.why: ANCHORLESS-SPEC 4.B.5: the currency the price is quoted in - how much of the move is gold rising and how much is the denominator falling

anchors.likely_source: the benchmark price deflated by FRED consumer prices - declare the arithmetic

anchors.likely_source: the same deflated series at its prior extreme, with the date it fell on
anchors.why: ANCHORLESS-SPEC 4.B.6: the historical mark the adjusted price is judged against. A valuation check with nothing to compare against is not a check - and with only about three independent episodes to compare, this disciplines the debate rather than settling it

anchors.likely_source: the World Gold Council's quarterly demand file (lagged)
anchors.why: ANCHORLESS-SPEC 4.B advisory

anchors.likely_source: London-New York price dislocations, dated
anchors.why: ANCHORLESS-SPEC 4.B advisory: physical-market stress signals

anchors.likely_source: World Gold Council / Metals Focus quarterly free summary
anchors.why: ANCHORLESS-SPEC 4.B advisory, and ONLY when miners are the subject - as a floor under gold it is a fiction, since costs run near 39 per cent of the price

gold.reading_rule: Official-sector buying is a SLOW series: it is published quarterly and runs two to five months behind. Its as-of date is rendered beside it at every sitting, so its age is read rather than assumed - a stale figure honestly dated is evidence; a stale figure read as current is not.

omitted.mining_cost_floor: Miners' all-in costs run near 39 per cent of the gold price. A floor 60 per cent below the market is not a floor - it is a statement about mining profits. It becomes relevant only when a MINING COMPANY is the subject, which is a different asset class.
omitted.lease_and_forward_rates: No free public benchmark exists: the London forward rate was discontinued in January 2015 and rates are now private dealer quotes.
omitted.ratio_of_anchor_metrics: Gold-to-equities and gold-to-inflation are quotients of figures the council already holds. Never anchor on the division of two anchors - it creates a way for a sitting to be refused over arithmetic.

seat_emphasis.advisor_bull: the official-sector bid: central-bank buying with its as-of date, the PBoC's reported figure beside the market's estimate of its true buying, and whether the bull case needs real yields to fall or can name the buyer paying up regardless.
seat_emphasis.advisor_base_rate: the outside view on real yields: what the five- and ten-year inflation-protected yields pay, what the textbook relationship says should follow, and how often it has actually proved true.
seat_emphasis.advisor_market_structure: who is setting the price now: fund holdings and monthly flows, speculative futures positioning, and the broad dollar as the denominator under the whole move.
seat_emphasis.advisor_risk: the asset's own risk: five-year realized volatility, the crowding in speculative positioning, and how much of the move would unwind if the fast money left.

commodity.note: ANCHORLESS-SPEC 4.C, the TEMPLATE for any standalone commodity, confirmed by the owner at freeze (AB15). A commodity is dug up, consumed and stored, so it genuinely runs short and long, and the market says so through inventories and the shape of the forward curve. It cannot be owned without cost or contract, so the council analyses it through the instrument it would actually buy (the owner's ruled product-conditional rule, W2.7).

anchors.likely_source: the executable contract price from the venue itself where it is free, or a dated mirror with a stated confidence note
anchors.why: ANCHORLESS-SPEC 4.C.1: the EXECUTABLE contract price - the price the trade could actually be done at, not an index

anchors.likely_source: the exchange the quoted contract trades on, named as a fact
anchors.why: ANCHORLESS-SPEC 4.C.1: the VENUE named. The tariff-era lesson is that a council anchoring on 'the price' without naming where it trades can build an entire case on a price it could not transact at

anchors.likely_source: the delivery month of the quoted contract, named as a fact
anchors.why: ANCHORLESS-SPEC 4.C.1: the CONTRACT MONTH named - a commodity has no single price, only a price for a date

anchors.why: ANCHORLESS-SPEC 4.C.2: the same product at a second benchmark. Where more than one exists, one price is not the price

anchors.condition: products quoted on more than one benchmark venue; declare the gap absent-by-design where only one benchmark exists
anchors.likely_source: the difference of the two venue prices - declare the arithmetic
anchors.why: ANCHORLESS-SPEC 4.C.2: how much of this price is the material and how much is policy. During the tariff episode the same metal traded at materially different prices in two places

anchors.likely_source: read OFF THE CURVE - the near and far contract prices, annualised over the intended holding period; declare both operands so the gate recomputes it
anchors.why: ANCHORLESS-SPEC 4.C.3: the carry over the intended holding period, read off the curve. Storage and financing are OBSERVED in the curve, never computed beside it - the market has already done that arithmetic

anchors.condition: products with an exchange stocks series; a product with no exchange stocks declares the reasoned gap (the ruled product-conditional item, W2.7)
anchors.likely_source: each venue's own published warehouse stocks, dated, one fact per venue with the venue in the id
anchors.why: ANCHORLESS-SPEC 4.C.4: exchange inventories SPLIT BY VENUE. During the tariff scramble total world inventory barely moved while each venue's number swung violently - a council reading one venue would have called relocation a shortage

anchors.likely_source: the last contract month with genuine liquidity on the named venue, stated in months
anchors.why: ANCHORLESS-SPEC 4.C.5: the tradable horizon. A three-year intent in a one-year-liquid contract makes the carry a forecast rather than an observation, and the record must say so

anchors.likely_source: the CFTC file or the venue's own series, dated
anchors.why: ANCHORLESS-SPEC 4.C.5: the roll requirement's evidence - how deep the contract actually is at the horizon the thesis needs

anchors.likely_source: subscription physical-premium services where purchased
anchors.why: ANCHORLESS-SPEC 4.C advisory: the fastest honest read on tightness, and the one paid source worth buying

anchors.likely_source: the USGS annual commodity summary as the free fallback; the paid cost curves otherwise
anchors.why: ANCHORLESS-SPEC 4.C advisory: promote to required only for horizons beyond five years, or where the case rests on supply responding

anchors.likely_source: the CFTC weekly file for the venue that reports it
anchors.why: ANCHORLESS-SPEC 4.C advisory: demoted for commodities because the reporting venue may be the distorted one - a partial view of a fractured market

commodity.capture_fragility: RECORDED, not solved: the only free London metals price and inventory feed is a scraped third-party mirror with no service guarantee - a single point of failure sitting under a required anchor. A sitting that must use it carries a stated confidence note on those facts, per the primary-or-discounted rule. A fallback path is REGISTERED, not built (ANCHORLESS-SPEC section 4.C).

omitted.demand_narratives: Grid spending, property and vehicle demand are the fashionable items and exactly what to leave out. In a storable commodity, demand reveals itself in inventories and in the curve, both already required; requiring the story on top double-counts it and gives a sitting a plumbing reason to fail while adding no measurement the price has not already made.
omitted.separate_storage_cost_inputs: The forward curve already prices storage and financing. Requiring separate inputs is arithmetic the market has done for us, and would be wrong more often than the curve.

bar_inputs.note: The three frozen facts the chairman's ladder is allowed to name. They are the class anchors themselves, named here in ONE place so the engine binds the ladder to the facts it claims rather than to any figure carried in the same unit: a funding rate is a percentage too, and a bar built on it instead of the bill rate rates a losing ladder hold (audit finding ANCHORLESS-B r1-4).

anchorless_rating.authority: ANCHORLESS-SPEC section 3 (owner rulings AB13.1-.3). The scaling rule and the band arithmetic are the builder's to fix IN DATA; every constant here is stated in the verdict and printed on the page, and the machine - never a seat - computes the arithmetic from them.
anchorless_rating.reading: The bar is CASH plus a premium scaled to the asset's own five-year realized volatility. Read it as a required reward for risk: bar_volatility_multiple is the minimum extra return per unit of the asset's own volatility that the council demands before it will call anything a buy. The bands above it are measured in the same volatility units, so one scaling step means the same thing everywhere.
bands: sell: the expected annualised result is below cash - the asset is expected to lose against a Treasury bill
hold: the expected annualised result clears cash but does not clear the bar decisively - it beats cash without paying for the risk taken
buy: the expected annualised result clears the bar by at least buy_excess_multiple times the asset's own five-year volatility
strong_buy: it clears the bar by at least strong_buy_excess_multiple times that volatility
monitor: the chairman judged the ladder too uncertain to aggregate, and said why - a watch-state, never a fifth opinion
anchorless_rating.sensitivity: ALWAYS printed (AB13.2): the probability at which the rating flips to the next rating down, and the bar recomputed one scaling step above and one below.

correction_reaudit.authority: Owner ruling AC15 (P8), unit U3d. A user correction that only NARROWS a claim needs no outside re-audit; a REBUILDING correction - one that changes what the seats reason from - requires a delta re-audit before the sufficiency gate passes. A correction is rebuilding when the corrected fact, or any figure struck from it, is one the business frame's reading rests on (cited in any section named below) or a headline pair (revenue, net income or operating cash flow against its prior-year pair). It narrows otherwise. A correction that brought a new fact or a new derived chain into the pack would also rebuild, but the correction command sets an existing, non-derived fact's value only and can produce neither. This list is DATA so a ruling can widen or narrow it without a code change - the discipline the revenue families already live under (owner ruling AC12.3).

period_basis.authority: Owner ruling AC15 (P3), unit U3d. An average must not be published as an annual figure. A derived fact that PRESENTS itself as an annual, per-year or run-rate figure - its id or label carries one of the signal words below - must declare which period it covers, and one that declares a multi-year or lifetime average basis while calling itself annual is refused: that is the conflation the owner flagged, a multi-decade average run rate read as the first twelve months' billing. The signal words and the average bases are DATA so a ruling can widen them without a code change. The set of legal bases is the capture contract's own period_basis enum; a fact struck by dividing a total by a term declares its basis by naming itself for what it is, which is what makes it, or keeps it from being, presented as annual.

archetype_measures.authority: Owner ruling AC15 (P2), unit U3e. The third canonical test declares the subject's ARCHETYPE - what kind of business it is - and the rating MEASURE that archetype calls for. This table is that rule as DATA, so a ruling can widen it without a code change - the discipline the revenue families and the correction re-audit rules already live under. The sufficiency gate enforces it for a single name only, and it never reads whether the declared archetype is TRUE (no machine can read a filing); it checks only that the measure matches the archetype, that the measure's numerator is present for the subject, and that the rating is computable for every peer - the peer numerator AND each denominator metric the rating_vs_history_or_peers row names in 'peer_denominator_metrics', all under the peer_<metric>__<ticker> convention - or the peer half is the declared 'peer_' gap (architect ruling 2026-09-20: a ratio is not computable from its numerator alone, so requiring only the peer numerator was too weak - a peer that carries enterprise value but no contracted capacity cannot be set beside the subject on enterprise value per contracted megawatt). The peer-side denominator ids differ by subject, so the capturer names them on the row rather than this table fixing them; for a profitable_operator the denominator is the earnings comparator (the price/earnings figure). The subject's own denominators are the frame's decisive metrics, whose ids differ by subject and so are not named here. Architect ruling 2026-09-20 (unit U3e, closing round-1 findings r1-1 and r1-3): 'computable' means BOTH halves of the ratio on BOTH sides, so each measure carries a 'denominators_required' count as DATA, and the rating_vs_history_or_peers row names that many 'subject_denominator_facts' (tier-1 fact ids) beside that many 'peer_denominator_metrics' (metric names). The sufficiency gate refuses a count that does not match the measure's, and holds each named subject denominator to the same bar as the numerator - a tier-1 reading, fresh, and a finite number; the peer half (its metric count and the per-peer denominators) is required only when no 'peer_' gap is declared. The capturer still names the facts; this table fixes only how many the measure needs.

profitable_operator.note: A business earning money, rated on earnings against its own history and its peers. The market value is the always-present anchor of an earnings multiple; the earnings side is the first canonical test's own facts (profit_growth), already required. denominators_required is 1: the earnings comparator (the price/earnings figure) is the one denominator the market value is divided by, named on the row's subject_denominator_facts for the subject and peer_denominator_metrics for the peers. That denominator is already a multiple (price over earnings), not an amount: the machine checks its presence, its freshness and that it is a number, and never divides the numerator by it (unit GROWTH-ARCHETYPE, D2).

ramping_infrastructure_builder.note: A business whose revenue has not arrived yet, rated on enterprise value per unit of contracted capacity and contracted revenue per unit - the TeraWulf finding. The contracted-capacity and rent-per-unit denominators are the frame's decisive metrics; their ids differ by subject. denominators_required is 2: both the contracted capacity and the contracted revenue per unit are named on the row's subject_denominator_facts for the subject and peer_denominator_metrics for the peers. The contracted revenue per unit is already a per-unit rate, not an amount: the machine checks its presence, its freshness and that it is a number, and never divides the numerator by it (unit GROWTH-ARCHETYPE, D2).

stabilised_lessor.note: A business earning steady rent on built-out capacity, rated on enterprise value to operating income. Operating income is the denominator, the frame's own decisive metric. denominators_required is 1: operating income is the one denominator enterprise value is divided by, named on the row's subject_denominator_facts for the subject and peer_denominator_metrics for the peers.

no_earnings_asset.note: An asset with no earnings - it keeps the AB13/AB15 anchorless ladder untouched, and this archetype is legal only for an anchorless subject. denominators_required is 0: the ladder is not a ratio and names no denominators; the subject_denominator_facts and peer_denominator_metrics checks do not run for an anchorless archetype.

financial_institution.note: Owner rulings AC28 and AC30 (unit FI-ARCHETYPE; research brief 2026-09-23). A business whose balance sheet is its product, or whose product is the stewardship of clients' capital: rated on the return it earns on the capital it is required to hold (a manager: the client capital entrusted to it) against the price the market pays for that capital. One archetype, six sub-types; the frame's fi_subtype selects the row below, and every key of that row is read exactly as a top-level archetype row is read. The numerator is the whole economic market value of the COMMON equity - every participating class and exchangeable unit, never the preferred - and a balance-sheet or manager sub-type divides it by TWO amounts, the capital base and the trailing earnings on it, so price-to-capital, price-to-earnings and the return on capital are struck from the same three facts for the subject and every peer. A financial holding divides by ONE, its net asset value, struck as a derived chain the nav_bridge declares. denominator_roles names what each subject denominator IS, in the order the rating row lists them; denominator_ids names, per role in the same order, the fact ids that role may be (architect ruling closing P-FIa-1, from the brief's per-sub-type rows), checked on the subject's denominators and the peers' denominator metrics alike - the continuing business's figure (fi_exited_business) carries the same id with its suffix.

bank.note: A deposit-funded lender, trader or custodian under a prudential capital rule. Denominators: tangible common equity at the latest quarter end, and net income applicable to common over the trailing four quarters (suggested ids tangible_common_equity, net_income_to_common_ttm; the capturer names them on the row).

insurer.note: A life, P&C or composite insurer. Denominators: the equity base the company's own operating return on equity divides by, and operating (core) net income attributable over the trailing four quarters (suggested ids equity_for_operating_roe, operating_earnings_ttm). Each peer on its own definition, the definition named in not_comparable_on.

reinsurer.note: A reinsurer. Denominators: shareholders' equity (tangible book for a US GAAP reporter) and net income attributable over the trailing four quarters (suggested ids equity_for_roe, net_income_ttm). A normal catastrophe year is shown by the large-loss budget/actual pair, never by a normalised figure.

traditional_asset_manager.note: A capital-light manager of long-only and index client assets. Denominators: assets under management at the latest quarter end, and as-adjusted net income over the trailing four quarters (suggested ids aum_period_end, adjusted_net_income_ttm).

alternative_asset_manager.note: A private-markets manager. The market value is struck on the economic share count including exchangeable units. Denominators: fee-earning assets at the latest quarter end, and fee-related earnings over the trailing four quarters (suggested ids fee_earning_aum_period_end, fre_ttm).

financial_holding.note: A holding company whose assets are mostly financial institutions. The one denominator is nav_total, a DERIVED chain: each listed stake at its market value, each unlisted holding at the company's reported value, plus holding-company cash less holding-company debt and preferred. The frame's nav_bridge names the parts; the discount's own history is the conditional nav_published_hist_/price_hist_ structure. The owned companies are not re-rated in the same sitting (AC30(3)).

float_compounder.note: An insurer that compounds its float - its share portfolio and wholly owned businesses outside insurance make up more than a third of its assets, or it reports those businesses as its own segments (owner ruling AC84(1)). Rated on price to book value - common shareholders' equity at the latest quarter end - read beside the growth of book value per share over ten financial year-ends with the dividends paid added back (AC84(2)); operating return on equity is shown, not rated. Book value already includes the share portfolio's gains, so the yardstick counts them once (AC84(3)). One denominator: the ten-year growth is read beside the yardstick, never divided by. The seventh sub-type.

reinvesting_grower.note: Owner ruling AC49(1) (unit GROWTH-ARCHETYPE; research brief 2026-09-24 section 2.1; owner rulings AC50 (1)-(11)). A listed company with real sales that has not yet had four profitable quarters, spending on growth: rated on what the market pays for its gross profit, read beside how fast its sales grow, with the months of cash left as a gate. The numerator is enterprise value (loss-makers often carry convertible debt or large net cash). Two denominators, both AMOUNTS over the trailing four quarters: gross profit and revenue, so enterprise value to gross profit, enterprise value to revenue and the gross margin strike from the same three facts for the subject and every peer; growth comes from the revenue_q pair. A listed company that earns most of its sales from a commodity it extracts under a recognised reserve standard, or from royalties and streams on others' output: rated on what the market pays per unit of its reserves, in the commodity's own unit, and for the last four quarters' operating cash flow, each printed beside the price it rests on - the price the reserves were counted at, the price the cash was earned at, today's price. The council never assumes an average price of its own. The numerator is enterprise value (net debt and clean-up obligations are declared operands where the capture strikes it). Two denominators, both AMOUNTS: the reserves and the trailing cash flow. On a model transition both are the continuing business's, the id ending in the row's continuing_suffix.

profitability_rule.why: Owner rulings AC49(1) and AC50 (1)-(3): a company without four profitable quarters behind it is rated on the growth path, never on earnings it does not yet have. A profitable quarter is one of the latest four with an operating profit under standard accounting, no adjustments - the operating income of that quarter above zero; a company that reports only every six months needs its latest two halves profitable. The rule works both ways: an archetype it governs refuses a company short of four profitable quarters and points at the growth archetype, and the growth archetype refuses a company with four, which has graduated to earnings. It governs the ordinary profit-maker and the landlord, turnarounds and cyclicals included; the contract-based infrastructure builder, the financial institution and an asset with no earnings are untouched. The quarters are the members of the quarterly floor below, read newest first by their period.

growth_runway.why: Owner rulings AC50(7) and AC50(8): the months of cash a growth company has left - cash plus short-term investments at the latest quarter end over the last four quarters' cash burn (operating cash flow less capital spending); undrawn credit lines are shown, never counted; a company not burning cash passes. Under the threshold the council rates it at most hold, sell still allowed, and the front of the report says so. The months are worked out by multiplication, never stored rounded (architect ruling A6).

resource_rule.why: Owner rulings AC51(R1, R4) and AC54(R13), architect ruling B8 (unit RESOURCE-ARCHETYPE): a company that reports reserves and earns from what it extracts is always rated as a producer - never on earnings at the top of the cycle, never as a growth company in a loss year. A single name whose pack carries any tier-1 fact whose id starts with reserve_prefix, and whose frame declares an archetype listed in refuses, is refused and pointed at the producer archetype. The producer steps outside the four-profitable-quarters rule by not being listed in profitability_rule.governs, as the financial institution does. No machine reads a filing: a capture that omits its reserves is the evidence auditor's to catch. The rule reads a capture made on or after applies_from.
resource_rule.reserve_history_why: The architect's ruling on P-RESOURCEa-2 (unit RESOURCE-ARCHETYPE, sub-charge b): a reserves_hist_ member is a past year-end's figure for the yardstick's own history, never a reported reserve on its own - wherever reserve_prefix is read, a fact starting with this prefix is set aside.

resource_rule.block_families_why: Architect rulings B4, B12 and lesson 1, owner rulings AC52(R8) and AC53(R11) (sub-charge b): every fact the resource_base block names under these fields starts with one of its field's prefixes - its reserve_facts with reserve_prefix and never reserve_history_prefix; a royalty or streaming company's fixed price paid per unit under each stream stands as its unit cost. The rated reserves denominator is among reserve_facts. The output and price-received fields read by family too (audit r1-6).
resource_rule.sales_natures_why: Owner ruling AC51(R1), the architect's ruling on P-RESOURCEa-11 (sub-charge b): a producer's sales come MOSTLY from what it extracts or from royalties and streams - the revenue lines of these natures carry more than half of revenue, read from each line's own share fact, else the sitting is refused naming the shares.
resource_rule.by_product_units_why: Owner ruling AC56(1), audit r1-1 of sub-charge b2, and the architect's ruling on P-RESOURCEb2-3 (the list stated as a class): a by-product off resource_products is shown apart in the one unit the company reports its reserve and output in, and that unit counts a physical quantity of the metal or the fuel - never money, a percentage or a count of shares. The list is a class: every unit a product on resource_products counts its reserves and output in, the oil and gas sub-type's boe_unit, and tonnes, each on allowed_units; a test in the evidence suite reads this membership from the data, so a quantity unit added elsewhere and forgotten here fails the suite instead of refusing a company.
resource_rule.by_product_price_unit_prefix_why: Architect ruling RESOURCE-ARCHETYPE(c2) fix round 2 under owner rulings AC56(1) and AC37: an off-list by-product price uses USD per its own reported quantity unit on by_product_units, never converted.
resource_rule.by_product_price_freshness_days_why: Architect ruling RESOURCE-ARCHETYPE(c2) fix round 2 and standing rule B4: today's price of an off-list by-product has the same three-day ceiling as every listed resource product.
resource_rule.reserve_max_age_why: Owner ruling AC53(R12): reserve figures are at most fifteen months old at the sitting, counted from the latest annual reserve report's own date; older, the sitting is refused with a shopping list. The five-year currency of a finished period (AC41(3)) does not apply to reserves, which are re-counted every year.
resource_rule.integrated_major_why: Owner ruling AC52(1) on AC51(R2): an integrated oil major - a large-scale energy company with significant operations across upstream production, midstream infrastructure, and downstream refining and marketing - is rated as an ordinary profit-maker, with its reserves and today's commodity price shown beside. A reserve-reporting company declared a profit-maker passes the rule both ways only with the frame's integrated_major block: its upstream and downstream arms each at or above integrated_major_min_share percent of the group's capital employed over the last three financial years combined, the midstream arm too where the company reports midstream as its own segment, and evidence of its own midstream assets always. Midstream is measured only where reported because the largest majors report pipelines inside their upstream and downstream segments. The downstream arm is refining and marketing: a chemicals arm is not downstream. Each arm's share fact is known by its id's prefix in integrated_major_arm_prefixes (architect ruling, session 2 of sub-charge a): a downstream share fact without the refining-and-marketing prefix is refused naming the arm and the id. A failed test refuses naming the arm and its figure.

forbidden_on_model_transition.why: Owner ruling AC15 (P2): rating a business that is CHANGING its model on trailing revenue drawn from the business it is exiting is explicitly forbidden - the WULF finding, where the headline revenue is mostly the segment being closed. Where the frame's what_is_changing.kind is 'model_transition' and the rating row rests on any fact id named here, the sufficiency gate refuses. Named as DATA so a ruling can widen the list without a code change: revenue_q and its prior-year pair are the whole-business trailing revenue; an EV-to-revenue multiple a capture strikes for the exited business is added here by id. Owner ruling AC28 (unit FI-ARCHETYPE) adds the revenue ids of a financial institution - net revenue, insurance revenue, gross written premiums and base fees, each with its prior-year pair - within the same meaning.
forbidden_on_model_transition.trailing_revenue_prefixes_why: Owner ruling AC49(1), architect ruling A9 (unit GROWTH-ARCHETYPE): the quarterly revenue family the growth archetype's floors carry is whole-business trailing revenue too, so any fact whose id starts with one of these prefixes is banned as the ids above are.

ladder_rules.ladder_instruction: A treasury company is rated over twelve months against cash (owner ruling AC92(2)): set horizon_months to 12. Write the coin scenarios, each scenario's coin price and odds, and the premium-case odds. Where the coin layer is cited, use its scenario names, coin prices and odds as recorded; where it is built, name at least three coin scenarios, each with one coin price. For every coin scenario name a case with 'premium falls' and a case with 'turns to a discount' in its name, each with its own odds above zero. A coin scenario's cells add up to its probability. Keep the existing answer form: the machine replaces premium and price_outcome in every premium-case cell, using your coin price, the in-force basis and the exact case premium. You write the odds and reasoning, not those two figures. Other cells keep their written premium and price. The chairman's check verifies the machine's arithmetic.

history_refusal.why: coins per share and the premium are required at every financial year-end since the company became a treasury company, from its own reports; a later annual report that is due must be read (owner rulings AC89(4), AC91(3))

raise_refusal.what: a dated record of every money raise in the last four quarters, or the declared absence of raises
raise_refusal.why: every money raise of the last four quarters is recorded — what was sold, the money raised and, for new shares, the figures that show whether coins per share rose or fell — or none is declared (owner ruling AC91(3))
raise_refusal.where: The company's share, bond and preferred-issue announcements for the last four quarters.

coin_sale_refusal.what: dated proceeds and the company's reason for every coin sale in the last four quarters, or the declared absence of sales
coin_sale_refusal.why: every coin sale of the last four quarters is recorded with the company's own words for why, or none is declared (owner ruling AC91(4))
coin_sale_refusal.where: The company's coin-disposal announcements and sale explanations in its reports.

fund_refusal.what: the named spot fund's NAV per share and price on the share price's day, or the ruled no-fund gap
fund_refusal.why: the coin's own listed spot fund is the plain alternative: its net asset value and price on the share price's day are required (owner ruling AC93; architect ruling R4)
fund_refusal.where: The named fund issuer's daily NAV and the fund's exchange price for that day.

peers_refusal.what: an empty treasury peer list and its declared peer gap
peers_refusal.why: a treasury company carries no peer section: the market is narrow and the owner looks only at the leading company for each coin (owner ruling AC92(4))
peers_refusal.where: The capture's business-frame peers list and peer_ gap declaration.

stray_refusal.what: a treasury-block entry matching this treasury fact, or a corrected fact key
stray_refusal.why: this fact is named as a treasury figure but the treasury block names no such coin, instrument, raise, sale, line or measure (owner rulings AC89(2), AC91(3))
stray_refusal.where: The capture's treasury coin, instrument, raise, sale, line and measure keys.

treasury.opening_shape_refusal_why: Owner rulings AC91(4), AC92(1): the opening records who chose each treatment and when.
treasury.preferred_keys_refusal_why: Owner ruling AC92(1): one choice per preferred, no other share.

paid_in_full.label: the dividend is paid in full

deferred.label: the dividend is deferred and still owed
deferred.why: The deferred case adds no cash within the ladder year and is allowed only when missed dividends accumulate (owner ruling AC92(3)).

missed.label: the dividend is missed and never paid
missed.why: The missed case adds no dividend cash and no dividend remains owed (owner ruling AC92(3)).

not_in_table_refusal.what: this preferred share in the issuer's own preferred-share table, named by its listed ticker
not_in_table_refusal.why: a listed preferred share is sat only on the terms the issuer's filings record for it, so its ticker must name exactly one preferred share in the issuer's table (owner rulings AC91(4), AC92(3))
not_in_table_refusal.where: the issuer's latest quarterly or annual report, its preferred-share note

other_issuer_refusal.what: an issuer that is a treasury company under the owner's rule
other_issuer_refusal.why: a listed preferred share is sat only where its issuer is a treasury company; every other preferred share and every bond stays parked (owner rulings AC49(2), AC92(3))
other_issuer_refusal.where: the issuer's capture, sat under the treasury-company rule

convertible_refusal.what: a preferred share that cannot be converted into the common share
convertible_refusal.why: this preferred share can be converted into the company's common share: a convertible preferred is a different instrument, refused until the owner rules on it (owner ruling AC92(3))
convertible_refusal.where: the preferred share's terms in the prospectus or the annual report

ranking_refusal.what: how this preferred share ranks against every other preferred share of the issuer, in the filings' own words
ranking_refusal.why: the cover counts every claim ranking ahead of this share and alongside it, and a ranking the filings do not state is never assumed (owner ruling AC92(3))
ranking_refusal.where: the prospectus or the annual report, the paragraph on ranking

record_refusal.what: every scheduled dividend of the last eight quarters, or since the share was listed, and whether each was paid, deferred or missed
record_refusal.why: a preferred share is judged on whether its dividend has been paid, and an incomplete record is never read as a clean one (owner ruling AC92(3))
record_refusal.where: the issuer's dividend announcements and its quarterly and annual reports

record_word_refusal.what: a dividend status the share's terms allow
record_word_refusal.why: a deferred dividend is one still owed, so only a share whose missed dividends accumulate can defer one; a share whose missed dividends do not accumulate misses them (owner rulings AC91(4), AC92(3))

young_refusal.what: a preferred share listed for at least a year
young_refusal.why: the preferred share has been listed for less than a year: its price swings cannot be measured over a year, and the council borrows no other swings (owner rulings AC92(2), AC92(3), AC78(4))
young_refusal.where: the exchange's listing notice or the prospectus

currency_refusal.what: a preferred share priced in the currency of the issuer's figures
currency_refusal.why: this preferred share is priced in another currency than the issuer's figures; one pack carries one currency, and a preferred share in another currency waits for the owner's ruling (owner rulings AC62(H16), AC65)
currency_refusal.where: the listing and the issuer's reports

applies_from_refusal.what: a capture made on or after the day the listed preferred rule applies
applies_from_refusal.why: the listed preferred share is ruled from this unit on; an earlier capture is never judged by it (owner ruling AC92(3))

price.why: The preferred's yield and ladder need its own fresh listed price (owner ruling AC92(3)).
price.what: the preferred share's latest listed price

par.why: The yearly dividend needs the stated amount per preferred share from its terms (owner ruling AC92(3)).
par.what: the preferred share's stated amount per share
par.where: The preferred share's prospectus or annual-report terms.

listed_on.why: The listing day sets the available swings history and dividend-record window (owner ruling AC92(3)).
listed_on.what: the preferred share's first listing day
listed_on.where: The exchange's listing notice or the preferred share's prospectus.

redemption_date.why: The redemption date comes from the terms, or a declared gap where the terms give none (owner ruling AC92(3)).
redemption_date.what: the first date the company may redeem this preferred share
redemption_date.where: The preferred share's redemption terms in the prospectus.

volatility.why: The ladder premium uses this preferred's own daily closes, never another share's swings (owner rulings AC92(3), AC78(4)).
volatility.what: the preferred share's own annual price swings
volatility.where: The preferred share's daily-close series and its swings calculation.

history_days.why: The trading-history day count proves whether this preferred has enough history for its own swings (owner rulings AC92(3), AC78(4)).
history_days.what: the number of days in the preferred share's trading history
history_days.where: The exchange's daily-close series for the preferred share.

window_days.why: The swings window uses the lesser of this preferred's whole history and the ruled full window (owner rulings AC92(3), AC78(4)).
window_days.what: the number of days used to measure the preferred share's price swings
window_days.where: The preferred share's swings calculation from its daily closes.

cash.why: The preferred's yield is compared with the pack's dated three-month bill cash anchor (owner ruling AC92(3)).
cash.what: the dated three-month Treasury bill rate
cash.where: The dated three-month Treasury bill rate source.

issuer_amount.why: The cover includes the issuer's recorded claim for this preferred series in the pack's currency (owner ruling AC92(3)).
issuer_amount.what: the issuer's total stated amount of this preferred series
issuer_amount.where: The issuer's preferred-share note in its latest quarterly or annual report.

issuer_dividend_rate.why: The exact yearly dividend uses the issuer's recorded rate, with that rate's date visible (owner ruling AC92(3)).
issuer_dividend_rate.what: the issuer's recorded yearly dividend rate for this preferred series
issuer_dividend_rate.where: The dividend-rate terms for this series in the issuer's latest filing.

ladder_words.ladder_instruction: Write the twelve-month ladder for the preferred share. In each scenario's dividend_cell name the dividend case - paid_in_full, deferred (only where missed dividends accumulate) or missed - the coin price you assume in twelve months, and the preferred share's own price then. The machine adds the dividends the case pays and works out the cover at your coin price; write price_outcome as your price plus those dividends. Give the paid-in-full case and at least one unpaid case a chance above zero.
ladder_words.chair_contract_lines: cover_read: one line, at most sixty words, reading the cover table - today and with the coin down 30, 50 and 70 percent - against the odds of your dividend cases.
ladder_words.cell_missing_refusal: every scenario names its dividend case, the coin price it assumes and the preferred share's price in twelve months (owner ruling AC92(3))
ladder_words.paid_case_refusal: the ladder carries a case where the dividend is paid in full, with a chance above zero (owner ruling AC92(3))
ladder_words.unpaid_case_refusal: the ladder carries at least one case where the dividend is not paid, with a chance above zero (owner ruling AC92(3))
ladder_words.cell_price_refusal: each scenario's price outcome is the preferred share's price plus the dividends its case pays in twelve months, worked out by the machine
ladder_words.read_missing_refusal: the chairman reads the cover table against his odds in one line (owner ruling AC92(3))
ladder_words.line_refusal: the chairman's cover line is one line of at most sixty words
ladder_words.read_on_other_kind_refusal: cover_read belongs to a listed preferred share only
ladder_words.cell_on_other_refusal: dividend_cell belongs to a listed preferred share's ladder only
ladder_words.deferred_case_refusal: a deferred dividend is one still owed, so only a share whose missed dividends accumulate can defer one; a share whose missed dividends do not accumulate misses them (owner rulings AC91(4), AC92(3))

casefile_words.cover_formula_words: The cover at a coin price: the coins it owns of the largest coin, %s, times that price, plus %s of other coins, plus cash of %s, divided by the claims ahead of this share, %s, plus the claims alongside it with this share included, %s (calculated).

listed_preferred.issuer_lead_why: An issuer refusal names the issuer before its unchanged treasury-company requirement (owner ruling AC92(3)).
listed_preferred.kind_line_words_why: The kind line names yield, own price swings and cover as the preferred's rating basis (owner ruling AC92(3)).

listed_preferred.true_debt_ranks_ahead_why: Every convertible bond and loan ranks ahead of every preferred share at face value in the cover (owner ruling AC92(3)).
listed_preferred.cover_falls_why: The cover shows today and the largest coin down thirty, fifty and seventy percent (owner ruling AC92(3)).

listed_preferred.record_grace_days_why: The completeness check allows ten extra days beyond the payment period (owner ruling AC92(3)).

listed_preferred.dividend_cases_why: The ladder distinguishes cash paid, dividends still owed and dividends never paid (owner ruling AC92(3)).
listed_preferred.statuses_why: Each scheduled payment records whether it was paid, deferred or missed (owner ruling AC92(3)).
listed_preferred.status_order_why: Each quarter shows its worst payment status, missed before deferred before paid (owner ruling AC92(3)).
listed_preferred.issuer_tables_why: The preferred evidence page reuses the issuer's debt, preferred and coin-sale tables without common-share calculations (owner ruling AC92(3)).

prose_figure_marks.why: Owner ruling AC19, unit U3f. The render-time scanner (council/evidence/trace.py) traces every number written into a business frame's prose to a recorded fact of the pack, allowing for rounding and for a change of scale or unit wording; a number that traces to nothing is MARKED where the prose is shown and the pack is NEVER refused for it. Every tolerance and every exemption the scanner uses lives here as data, not as a constant in the code (AC19(4)).
prose_figure_marks.relative_tolerance_note: The fallback match when the prose number and a fact value do not agree to the prose's own significant figures: they still match when they are within this fraction of each other.
prose_figure_marks.year_note: A four-digit integer in this range, standing on its own, is a year and is never marked.
prose_figure_marks.day_note: A plain integer in this range sitting directly beside a month word is the day of a written date and is never marked, with one exception: a day written AFTER its month ('September 30') is only a date's day when nothing that could be its unit follows it (see date_day_closers) - a following unit word ('September 30 MW') makes it a measured figure that is still marked (architect ruling closing register item P-U3f-2, audit UPGRADE2-U3f r3-1). A percent, currency or scaled figure that merely follows a month name is a figure of the prose and is still marked; a month-year is caught by the year rule (audit UPGRADE2-U3f r2-2).
prose_figure_marks.plain_count_note: A plain integer from 0 to this ceiling, with no currency sign, percent or scale, is a count and is never marked.
prose_figure_marks.date_day_closers_note: For a day written AFTER its month ('September 30'), the day is a written date's day only when the next non-space character after it (and any ordinal suffix) is the end of the text, one of these closers, or the first digit of a four-digit year. Any other following word makes the number a measured figure that is still marked (architect ruling closing register item P-U3f-2, audit UPGRADE2-U3f r3-1). The day-before-month order ('30 September') is unaffected: the month word itself follows the number.
prose_figure_marks.scale_words_note: The power of ten a scale word or letter written directly after a number multiplies it by. Read case-sensitively for the single letters (M is millions) and case-insensitively for the words.
prose_figure_marks.percent_words_note: Words after a number that make it a percentage (the percent SIGN and the two words 'per cent' are read by the scanner directly). A percentage matches a percent-unit or fraction-unit fact, never a plain one.
prose_figure_marks.month_words_note: A plain day-of-month integer (see day_min/day_max) sitting directly beside one of these is the day of a written date and is never marked; the year of a month-year is caught by the year rule. For the day-after-month order ('September 30') a following unit word lifts the exemption - see date_day_closers_note.
prose_figure_marks.currency_scale_units_note: A recorded fact whose unit states a currency scale is read in base units by this power of ten before it is compared to a prose number; a unit not listed here (USD, USD_per_share, MW, years, x) is read at its face value. Architect dispatch P-LISTINGS-2 under AC59(1) and AC37(1): every allowed currency magnitude follows the USD pattern.

The foundations calendar test reads these earliest years from the floors; all twelve lists reach 2027. The earlier US and continuous-trading calendars keep their existing rules.
price_series.min_bars_note: The subject's series carries at least this many daily bars (about two trading years), or declares its gap - a recent listing has no longer history. A benchmark series follows the same rule and must also span the subject's window.
price_series.max_gap_note: No two consecutive bars may lie more than this many calendar days apart, not counting the days the series' exchange calendar below declares a holiday. A normal weekend is three days; a long weekend four.
price_series.max_staleness_note: The last bar lies at most this many exchange days before the capture's date. An exchange day is a weekday the series' calendar trades (its trading_weekdays, ISO numbering, Monday 1 to Sunday 7) that the calendar does not declare a holiday; on the all-days calendar every calendar day counts. A series naming a calendar the floors do not define refuses.
price_series.calendars_by_asset_class_note: The calendars an UNLISTED subject's price series may name, by its asset class (architect ruling closing P-U4a1-5): a spot coin trades every day. A subject with a listing is bound by calendars_by_listing instead, whatever its shape. An unlisted subject whose class is not listed here (bullion, a contract with no listing recorded) has no calendar defined and its price series refuses until one is added here, as data. The benchmark series is bound by its benchmark's listing through calendars_by_listing (architect ruling closing P-U4a1-8).
price_series.calendars_by_listing_note: The calendar a LISTED subject's price series must name, by its listing (architect ruling closing P-U4a1-5): a stock, a fund, or a basket or theme whose members list, trades on its exchange's calendar whatever it holds - a US-listed fund holding coins trades on the US calendar. Matched ignoring case and extra spaces, whole name only. A listing not named here refuses: add the exchange and its calendar (with the calendar's holidays below) as data before the first sitting that carries such a series. freshness_ceiling.authority: Owner ruling AC41(3), unit SITTING-FIXES. A fact that is a dated record of a finished period - a first guide for a closed period, a filed annual report, a closed quarter's figures - counts as current for up to five years from its own date; after that it is too old to carry. Prices, balances and anything that moves keep their short freshness rules. No tier-1 fact may be ruled current for longer than this; the provenance gate refuses a longer rule by name.

rounded_quotient_families.authority: Owner ruling AC41(2), unit SITTING-FIXES (architect ruling on audit finding r1-1). A calculated share or yield whose division does not come out even may be recorded rounded once, half-up, shown as rounded - an amendment to AB10's exact-decimal rule for that one kind. The gate accepts a rounded quotient only for a fact whose id starts with one of `prefixes` or contains one of `contains`, and only where its arithmetic declares `rounded_places`; every other quotient stays exact. The share families are the ids a revenue line's share of the period is struck under (the worked example's `segment_revenue_share_`, and any id naming `share_of_period`); the yield family is any id carrying `yield`. AC88(1) extends the rounded quotient rule to the daily uranium spot proxy, rounded once to the cent.
